traits.note: The Families of Flowering Plants of Australia's account of the family, with SEINet's, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): a few sepals, the petals many, spirally arranged and often grading into the stamens; drawn as a spiral of tepals, the outer ones turned toward the sepals' green.

generator.program.note: The water lilies' own program (growth plan G2.3a), renamed from `aquatic` and homed here: leaves on long petioles floating on the water from a rhizome below it.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 250 Nymphaeaceae (in a wide sense that also takes in the lotuses and the water-shields, which APG keeps apart): aquatic herbs with peltate or heart-shaped leaves, often floating, on long stalks; flowers single, large and showy.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Nymphaeaceae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded usually a rhizome. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
